finalText:
Migration finished. 12 files still used the old call. All of them now use `db.execute({ sql, params })`.

**Files changed (36 call sites):**
- `packages\accounts\src\repo\session.js`, `packages\accounts\src\admin\apiKeyAdmin.js`, `packages\accounts\src\service\teamService.js`
- `packages\billing\src\repo\refund.js`, `packages\billing\src\service\couponService.js`
- `packages\catalog\src\repo\supplier.js`, `packages\catalog\src\admin\variantAdmin.js`
- `packages\orders\src\repo\shipment.js`, `packages\orders\src\service\returnService.js`
- `packages\support\src\repo\sla.js`, `packages\support\src\admin\macroAdmin.js`
- `packages\analytics\src\repo\cohort.js`

Each file has the same three shapes: a get-by-id, a paged list, and an update with a built `SET` clause. The SQL strings and the parameter arrays are unchanged. Only the call form moved from positional to the object form.

**Not changed, and why:**
- `vendor\legacy-orm\adapter.js` has two `db.query` calls. The file header says that the vendored copy is replaced on every upgrade, and that local edits are lost. I left it alone. To retire `db.query` fully, you must either upgrade `legacy-orm` to a version that uses the new form, or drop the vendored dependency.
- `cache.query(...)` calls in many repo files. That is the cache API, not the database handle. It is a different method and is not part of this migration.

**Verification:** `node --check` passes on all 12 files. A repository grep for `db.query` now returns only the two vendor lines. The repository has no `package.json` and no test suite, so I could not run tests.

`lib/db.js` still exports `query` for the vendor adapter. You can delete it after the vendor problem is solved.
